review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. IPHC and NOAA sources support demersal depth and seasonal migration; reported adult temperatures are bottom-water temperatures and cannot validate satellite SST.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for pacific halibut.
factors.value_notes: IPHC reports Pacific halibut routinely occupy bottom-water temperatures around 3-8 °C, but the fish is demersal and the model factor is satellite sea-surface temperature. Bottom temperature is not interchangeable with SST, and the reviewed sources do not validate the configured 5-13 °C surface-temperature band or 7-11 °C ideal. Keep values unchanged and mark needs_source.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for pacific halibut.
factors.value_notes: IPHC reports summer feeding on the continental shelf to about 500 m, most frequent captures around 30-270 m, and deeper offshore winter spawning. NOAA/USGS sources describe ontogenetic depth shifts, including juveniles in shallow water and spawning at roughly 183-457 m. The configured 20-250 m band covers much feeding habitat but does not represent the full life-stage or winter spawning depth range.
